newsitem.title: USA: Outright U.S. cash crudes slip on gasoline retreat.
newsitem.headline: Outright U.S. cash crudes slip on gasoline retreat.

text.p: U.S. cash crude prices slouched in a gasoline-led price retreat on Monday morning, though domestic grades attracted deals for sweet barrels at unchanged levels.

September West Texas Intermediate/Cushing stood 25-30 cents lower at $19.75-85 a barrel. September/October spreads widened slightly to -25 cents, pushing Postings Plus levels to around $1.82-87, traders said.

Trades were achieved in the Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James market at 23 cents over the benchmark, with the Midland/WTI selling at -30 cents. Both trades were steady from Friday, reflecting the stagnant state for grade differentials.

Other levels had Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at either side of a 25 cents discount to the benchmark, and West Texas Sour/Midland around $1.20-30 under WTI. Eugene Island barrels failed to move from a $1.20-30 discount.
The return of refinery units shut in the previous weeks have remained key to outright price movement, traders said.

Indeed, the expected return to normal operations at Tosco's Bayway refinery in New Jersey over the weekend depressed the NYMEX energy complex. The plant's catalytic cracker had been downed for repairs.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline slipped some 1.50 cents a gallon on the Tosco situation, traders said.
The 45,000 barrel per day (bpd) reformer at Venezuela's Cardon refinery was still running at minimum throughput on Monday after a problem emerged Friday in the catalyst generator.

Also, a planned stoppage at Ecuador's main Esmeraldes oil refinery was extended two weeks, pushing the restart date from August 18 to September 1. Capacity at the facility is being upped from 90,000 bpd to 110,000 bpd.
